ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because the bust is itself a combo resource: you pick who gets Seized (Squacco as fall guy, Slipway Champion to replay three Runs) and buy it back bigger, so every turn has a real order-your-Runs puzzle.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because no current tribe, nor a generic auto-battler one, has a push-your-luck gauge with two opposite payoffs (land exactly on the Limit, or go over on purpose) on the same Heat.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken, but two rules the combo play depends on (Run order, Grisel's Tag count) need one clear line each.

points.text: Grisel's stolen enemy copy is 'Tagged', but her text also says Seized units gain two Tags; say whether the stolen copy gets one Tag or two.
Johnny's main trick is choosing which unit Runs last, but the order of several Start of Turn Runs isn't stated; say they go in reading order (or player's choice) so the trick can be planned.
Squacco plus Hackle plus Grisel is a cheap every-turn loop (rebuy for 2, two Tags, team +1/+1); lovely, but it lives off one T3 card, so a second fall-guy option at T4 or T5 would widen it.
Lantern Signaller ignores the Heat game; tying its target to the roll (more units on a 3) would make it pull towards Tibby or away from him.
Hothead and Nyx only read Heat; one hot payoff that reads the number of times you were Caught this game would give the Hot build its own Nan Silverholt.

standouts.why: Slipway Champion is the perfect thing to get Seized on purpose: it comes back Tagged and replays three Runs.
Sergeant Squacco turns the bust into a choice of victim, which is the heart of the combo play.
Close-Shave Creeler with Pebble Jack makes landing exactly on the Limit a skill shot worth double.

weakest.why: Salt-Pan Runner is plain gold with a Run sticker; it does the obvious job.
Lantern Signaller is a generic random buffer that doesn't care about Heat.
Holt Kit is a fine seed but a one-line Clean check with no twist.

flags.note: With Hackle and Grisel, Squacco gains two Tags every turn for 2 gold; linear, but worth the owner's eye.
Tag count on the stolen enemy copy is ambiguous.
Creel-Weaver with Pilot and Moss adds three tier-up units a turn; may pull the curve a tier early.
